description: A tree of riverbank, floodplain (varzea), secondary/gaps, 20-40 m tall (to 48 m). Straight cylindrical trunk, light coloured, sometimes pinkish (Spanish Wikipedia); bole free of branches up to 18 m, some basal swellings but no well-developed buttresses (Useful Tropical Plants, src 3). Rounded, dense crown (TTSM src 0, Spanish Wikipedia); 'broadly rounded or elongate' (Useful Tropical Plants). Fruit: kidney-shaped drupe (nut) 2.5-3.5 x 1-2 cm, hanging from a curved, fleshy, S-shaped receptacle.

notes: Template shorea_leprosula: an emergent: a buttressed clear bole under an umbrella crown (light red meranti). Briefly deciduous by the sources, but no months given: drawn evergreen. NOT SOURCED (the template's or a default value): crown width (the template's ratio); crown depth (the template's); leaf colour (a tropical evergreen's mid green). Research notes: Leaf habit: Spanish Wikipedia says partly deciduous, leaves yellowing then dropping partly in the dry season and replaced at the start of the rains; English Wikipedia calls it evergreen; TTSM (Fournier, Costa Rica) notes flushes of new foliage in January, then flowers through April (citing Jimenez et al. 1996). No source gives leafless months. Spanish Wikipedia: flowers and fruits Feb-May, fruit ripe Mar-May. Months are Costa Rica/Central America, not Osa-specific. Leaf size: 15-30 x 5-12 cm (en and es Wikipedia description); es Wikipedia habitat section 10-35 x 4-12 cm; leaves clustered at twig ends, obovate, apex rounded, notched or acute. Leaf colour and texture not found. Height: 20-40 m (es Wikipedia), 45 m (TTSM), 48 m (en Wikipedia). dbh max: TTSM 3 m d.b.h.; Useful Tropical Plants up to 200 cm. Habitat: TTSM, often dominant on flood plains and in gallery forests; Useful Tropical Plants, secondary forest, stream sides, sometimes pure stands, young plants need sun and are seldom in mature woodland (basis for 'light-demanding'). The monkey and bat records are Croat's Flora of Barro Colorado (Panama), quoted on the HVAA Symbiota page; the source names them 'white-faced and howler monkeys' and I added the scientific names. Bats eat only the fleshy receptacle and drop the nut (Wikipedia).
